stories.headline: US Embassy Abuja and Lagos consulate shut 26–27 November
stories.summary: The US Mission in Nigeria says its embassy in Abuja and consulate in Lagos are closed on Thursday 26 and Friday 27 November for the American Thanksgiving holiday. No consular or visa appointments will be served on those two days, and normal work is expected to resume the following week.
stories.tip: If your interview or passport pickup fell on 26 or 27 November, check your appointment account and rebook through the official US visa portal only, not through an agent.

stories.headline: Canada's Express Entry gives job offers points again, no LMIA needed
stories.summary: Since 3 November, Express Entry has a new 'labour market integration' score worth up to 150 points. A job offer in a high-wage occupation now earns 50, 70 or 100 points depending on how well the job pays, and it no longer needs an LMIA; Canadian work experience in such jobs can score instead, but you get only the higher of the two. On 25 November IRCC invited 6,000 French speakers with a cut-off score of 401, the second draw under the new system.
stories.tip: Check if your occupation is on IRCC's high-wage list, and walk away from anyone selling a 'Canada job offer' — officers check that offers are genuine.

stories.headline: Australia's SkillSelect moves into ImmiAccount on 28 November
stories.summary: Home Affairs has taken SkillSelect offline from 24 to 27 November while it moves into ImmiAccount, with the new system going live on 28 November. Submitted expressions of interest for 189, 190 and 491 skilled visas stay valid, and invitations still inside their 60-day window can be opened in the new portal. Unsubmitted draft EOIs cannot be carried over.
stories.tip: If you only had a draft EOI, create an ImmiAccount and start a fresh EOI from 28 November; if yours was already submitted, import it to keep track of it.
stories.source: Department of Home Affairs / EIG Law

stories.headline: Canada approved 24% fewer visitor visas for Nigerians this year
stories.summary: New IRCC figures show Canada approved 26,210 visitor visas for Nigerians between January and August 2026, down from 34,360 in the same months of 2025, even though total approvals worldwide rose by about 11%. Nigeria still ranks fifth among source countries, and August alone was better than a year earlier. IRCC's latest estimate puts a visitor visa decision for applicants in Nigeria at about 98 days, while study permits take about 11 weeks.
stories.tip: Apply for a Canadian visitor visa at least four months before your trip, and show a clear reason to return home, such as a job, business or family ties, with documents to back it up.

stories.headline: UK judged 84% of interviewed Nigerian students not credible
stories.summary: A UK Visas and Immigration briefing seen by The PIE News shows caseworkers found 9,043 of the 11,415 student visa applicants they interviewed between May and October 2026 not credible. For Nigerian applicants the figure was 84%, behind only Nepal and India, and the share of Nigerians called for interview jumped from 7% in 2025 to 21% this year. The most common weak points were little research into the university, not explaining why the UK and the course fit future plans, poor course knowledge, English level and doubts about funds.
stories.tip: Before your credibility interview, be ready to explain in your own words why you chose this university, course and the UK, how it fits your career, and exactly where your money comes from.

stories.headline: New Zealand's six-month graduate work visa is now open
stories.summary: Since 16 November 2026, international graduates of Level 5 to 7 courses in New Zealand who studied full-time for at least 24 weeks, but whose qualification doesn't qualify for a Post-Study Work Visa, can apply online for a Short-Term Graduate Work Visa. It gives six months of open work rights to job-hunt and move to an employer-sponsored visa, and you need at least NZ$5,000 to support yourself. You must apply within three months of your student visa ending, you get only one, and English, foundation and bridging courses don't count.
stories.tip: If your NZ student visa ended after 16 August 2026 or ends soon, check your qualification level and apply through Immigration Online before the three-month window closes.

stories.headline: UK student visa funds go up on 30 November
stories.summary: From Sunday 30 November, UK student visa applicants must show more money for living costs: £1,570 a month for study in London (up from £1,529) and £1,203 a month elsewhere (up from £1,171), for up to nine months. The change comes from the Home Office's September statement of changes (HC 584). Applications made before 30 November are judged on the old amounts.
stories.tip: If your CAS and bank statement are ready, submit before 30 November to use the lower figure; if not, make sure your account shows the new amount for the full 28 days before you apply.

stories.headline: Nigeria to print its own passport booklets from May 2027
stories.summary: Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo broke ground on 20 November on a $70 million passport booklet factory at the Nigeria Immigration Service headquarters in Abuja, and said local production should start by May 2027. The plant is meant to make six million e-passport booklets a year at first, well above Nigeria's yearly need of about two million, so booklet shortages caused by foreign suppliers and exchange rates should ease. It is privately funded under a concession, and the new factory alone does not promise faster processing.
stories.tip: Don't wait for the new factory: if your passport expires within the next year, renew now through the NIS contactless portal, because many embassies want at least six months' validity.

stories.headline: Australia tightens travel permission for sponsored workers waiting on visas
stories.summary: Home Affairs says Bridging Visa B applications lodged from 30 November 2026 by people waiting on an employer-sponsored visa will get travel periods that match the actual trip, not the long periods of up to a year or more that were common. Applicants must give a real reason, dates and evidence, and a general 'holiday' or 'visiting family' line may not be enough. The law is not changing, only how strictly officers apply it, and a trip that runs past the approved period ends the BVB.
stories.tip: If you are on a bridging visa in Australia and plan to visit Nigeria for Christmas, lodge your BVB before 30 November or 2 weeks to 3 months before you fly, with evidence of your trip, and don't buy a non-refundable ticket until it is granted.

stories.headline: Ireland tells residents travelling at Christmas to renew IRP cards early
stories.summary: Immigration Service Delivery says Irish Residence Permit renewals are taking about six to nine weeks because of high demand, and the new card can take up to two more weeks to arrive. It cannot promise a card in time for holiday travel, and emergency re-entry visas are only for genuine emergencies, not planned trips. Your new permission still starts from the old card's expiry date, so applying early costs you nothing.
stories.tip: If your IRP card expires before or during a Christmas trip home, apply online for renewal today and keep your proof of application with you.

stories.headline: UKVI tells eVisa holders to check nationality and date of birth
stories.summary: UK Visas and Immigration emailed eVisa holders on 16 November after a review found that, in a small number of cases, the nationality or date of birth on an eVisa did not match the Home Office record. eVisas and share codes now show the verified record, and UKVI says permission, expiry dates and conditions such as the right to work and rent are not affected. It did not say how many people were hit.
stories.tip: Log in to your UKVI account, confirm your nationality, date of birth and linked passport are correct before you travel or start a new job, and use the GOV.UK eVisa error form if anything is wrong.

stories.headline: New Zealand visa portal down Sunday after Microsoft outage pushed upgrade back a week
stories.summary: Immigration New Zealand says many online visa applications, including student, most visitor, AEWV and partner or child of a worker or student visas, cannot be started or continued from 08:00 to 23:59 NZ time on Sunday 22 November. Some others, including partner or child of a New Zealander visas, go offline briefly between 06:00 and 08:00 on Monday 23 November. The upgrade was first planned for 15–16 November but slipped a week after a global Microsoft outage disrupted INZ systems.
stories.tip: If you are applying to New Zealand this weekend, submit before Saturday night Nigerian time or wait until Monday, and save your form often so you do not lose work.

stories.headline: Canada counts stipend-paid professor and postdoc work for Express Entry
stories.summary: IRCC has changed the Express Entry category for researchers with Canadian work experience. Work as a university professor, lecturer or postdoctoral researcher (NOC 41200) now counts even when it is paid through stipends, grants, bursaries or scholarships, and it can earn CRS points. Teaching and research assistant jobs (NOC 41201) no longer qualify for this category.
stories.tip: If you are a postdoc or lecturer in Canada paid by stipend or grant, update your Express Entry profile to list that experience under NOC 41200.

stories.headline: German mission: you don't need a paid flight ticket to apply for a visa
stories.summary: The German Mission in Nigeria said on X on 18 November that applicants do not have to buy a flight ticket before applying for a German visa. Depending on the visa checklist, a flight reservation or a proposed travel itinerary is enough. The post was the last in its series busting claims made by visa agents.
stories.tip: Check the checklist for your visa type on the German Missions in Nigeria website, submit a reservation or itinerary, and buy the actual ticket only after your visa is issued.
stories.source: Chronicle NG / German Mission in Nigeria

stories.headline: US judge blocks new limits on student internships (CPT)
stories.summary: A federal judge in Boston has stopped the Department of Homeland Security from enforcing two August 2026 directives that narrowed curricular practical training (CPT), the work placements F-1 students do as part of their course. Under the directives, a placement only counted if every student in the programme had to do it, which shut out elective internships taken for credit. The order is a preliminary injunction, so the case continues and the government could still appeal.
stories.tip: If you are on an F-1 visa and a CPT placement was cancelled or put on hold, ask your school's international student office (your DSO) whether it can now be authorised again.

stories.headline: Australia visitor visas lodged from 28 November will carry 'No Further Stay'
stories.summary: From 28 November 2026, condition 8503 ('No Further Stay') becomes compulsory on Australian Visitor (subclass 600) tourist and business visas, as well as ETA and eVisitor visas. Anyone holding such a visa will generally be unable to apply for another visa, such as a student or work visa, while inside Australia. It only covers applications lodged on or after 28 November, and a waiver is possible only after a major change in circumstances you could not have foreseen.
stories.tip: If you want to study or work in Australia, apply for that visa from Nigeria; do not plan to enter as a visitor and switch, and lodge any visitor application you have ready before 28 November.

stories.headline: New international students at US universities down 15% this autumn
stories.summary: The Institute of International Education says US colleges hosted about 1.15 million international students in 2025/26, but its autumn 2026 snapshot of more than 800 institutions shows total international enrolment down 9% and new enrolment down 15%. The fall in graduate numbers came mainly from fewer master's students. Most Nigerians cannot get new US student visas while the January 2026 suspension remains in place.
stories.tip: If the US is closed to you for now, compare UK, Canadian, Irish or German master's options and their intake deadlines rather than waiting on a US place.

stories.headline: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships for UK master's close 8 December
stories.summary: Applications are open for the 2027/28 Commonwealth Shared Scholarships, which pay for a one-year master's at a UK university starting in September or October 2027, and Nigerians are eligible. The award covers full tuition, a return flight and a monthly living allowance of £1,712, or £2,000 in the London area. The closing time is 16:00 GMT on 8 December 2026.
stories.tip: Apply through the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission's own site, check that your chosen university and course are on the shared scholarship list, and submit well before 8 December.
stories.source: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK

stories.headline: US says it has cancelled over 6,000 visas linked to birth tourism
stories.summary: The US State Department's Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force says it has now revoked more than 6,000 visas held by people who travelled to give birth in America so the child gets US citizenship, or who helped arrange such trips. A month earlier the figure was about 4,000, and the department says it is still identifying others. It did not say how many of those affected were Nigerian.
stories.tip: Never use a US visitor visa to travel for childbirth or to help someone else do so; it can cost you the visa and future applications.

stories.headline: German embassy in Abuja closes visa section for December and January
stories.summary: Germany's embassy in Abuja says its visa section will be shut through December 2026 and January 2027 because of building work. During that time, visa applicants who would normally go to Abuja must apply at the German Consulate General in Lagos. No exact reopening date was given, and it is not clear whether Lagos will release extra appointments to cover the demand.
stories.tip: If you live in the North and need a German visa before February, book a Lagos appointment early and budget for the trip.

stories.headline: US court strikes down four-year cap on student visa stays
stories.summary: A federal judge in Massachusetts has thrown out the Homeland Security rule that would have given F-1 students, J-1 exchange visitors and foreign journalists a fixed admission period instead of 'duration of status'. The court had already paused the rule in September, and on 16 November it cancelled it completely. For now, students can stay as long as they keep studying full time on a valid I-20, but the government can still appeal.
stories.tip: Keep your I-20 and SEVIS record current and talk to your school's international office before planning around any fixed end date, as an appeal could change things.

stories.headline: British High Commission warns Nigerians: nobody can guarantee a UK visa
stories.summary: The British High Commission in Nigeria has told applicants that no agent, person or company can promise a successful UK visa. It says any offer of guaranteed approval by email, phone call or social media is a scam. Applications should only be made through the official GOV.UK website.
stories.tip: Apply only on GOV.UK, never pay anyone who promises approval, and report suspicious offers before sending money or documents.

stories.headline: Australia's Training visa (407) now only for applicants outside Australia
stories.summary: From 12 November 2026, a new application for Australia's Training visa (subclass 407) is only valid if you lodge it while outside Australia, and you must also be outside Australia when the visa is granted. An application made from inside Australia under the new rule is treated as invalid and gets no bridging visa, even if the online system accepts it. Valid applications lodged before 12 November are still decided under the old rules, and existing 407 visas are not cancelled.
stories.tip: If an employer offers you a 407 training place, make sure their nomination is approved first, then lodge from Nigeria and wait there for the decision.

stories.headline: Australia stops graduates adding family to 485 visas later
stories.summary: From 13 November 2026, partners and children can only be included in a Temporary Graduate (subclass 485) visa if they apply together with the graduate in one combined application. In most cases they must already have been on the graduate's Student or 485 visa as dependants, or be a child born after that visa was granted; joining later as a subsequent entrant is no longer possible. Applications lodged before 13 November are decided under the old rules.
stories.tip: If you are studying in Australia and plan to bring a spouse or child, add them to your Student visa now and lodge your 485 together with them.

stories.headline: Ireland's work permit portal stays offline after security breach
stories.summary: Ireland's Employment Permits Portal has been shut since late October after the Department of Enterprise found unauthorised activity on the system, and it has missed its planned reopening date. Applications already submitted are still being decided, but new applications cannot be sent by email while the department prepares temporary arrangements. Officials say people whose renewals or deadlines are delayed by the outage will get flexibility, and that only names, email addresses and account roles appear to have been exposed.
stories.tip: Watch for fake emails or texts about your permit: the department says it never asks for personal details that way, so send urgent questions only to epos@enterprise.gov.ie.
stories.source: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment (Ireland)

stories.headline: Canada sets aside 45,000 extra PR places for spouses of Canadians in 2027
stories.summary: IRCC says it will use extra permanent residence spaces in 2027 to clear applications that are already waiting, including up to 45,000 for spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who live in Canada. A further 100,000 places will go to workers already in Canadian communities, chosen with the provinces. No new programme is opening, and people who have already applied do not need to contact IRCC.
stories.tip: If your spousal PR file is pending, keep your address, passport and contact details up to date in your IRCC account so nothing slows it down.

stories.headline: Canada makes its rural immigration route to PR permanent
stories.summary: Canada has turned its Rural Community Immigration Pilot into a permanent programme, with 5,500 admission spaces planned in the 2027-2029 levels plan. The 14 current communities, including Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Brandon and Moose Jaw, stay in, and more will be added later. Candidates still need a job offer from an employer the community has designated, plus a community recommendation.
stories.tip: Only trust job offers you can match to the community's official list of designated employers, and never pay anyone for a 'rural job offer'.

stories.headline: UK student visa applications down 20% in a year, care worker applications down 61%
stories.summary: Home Office figures released on 12 November show 349,900 student main applications in the year to October 2026, 20% fewer than a year earlier, while student dependant applications fell 32%. Skilled Worker applications dropped 42% and Health and Care Worker applications fell 61%. The cuts follow tighter rules on dependants, salaries and overseas care recruitment.
stories.tip: Fewer applicants does not mean easier approval: prepare full funds proof and a clear study plan, and check your university is still sponsoring Nigerian students.

stories.headline: New Zealand won't grant parents residence while a child is unlawful
stories.summary: Immigration New Zealand says that for residence applications lodged from 12 November 2026, a parent or other secondary applicant cannot be approved while a dependent child is in the country without a valid visa. The child must first get a proper visa or leave New Zealand, and dropping the child from the application does not get around the rule. Applications lodged before 12 November are decided under the old rules.
stories.tip: If any child in your family has an expired New Zealand visa, sort out their status before you lodge a residence application.

stories.headline: Nearly half of Nigerian Schengen visa applications refused in 2025
stories.summary: A Foreign Affairs ministry analysis reported by Sunday Punch and BusinessDay puts Nigeria's Schengen refusal rate at 46.9% in 2025, with Belgium, Spain and France refusing the most. Failed Schengen applications alone cost Nigerians about €11.5 million in fees that are never refunded. The same report puts UK refusals at 35.4% in early 2026 and Canadian study permit refusals at about 75%.
stories.tip: Before paying any visa fee, check that your bank statements, ties to Nigeria and travel plan clearly match the visa you are asking for.

stories.headline: Germany's Lagos consulate to add visa counters before year end
stories.summary: Germany's Consul General in Lagos, Daniel Krull, said on 6 November that the consulate will open more visa counters before the end of 2026 and work with outside service providers to release more appointments. More files will also be sent to a German processing centre in Europe to cut delays. A document checking centre for Nigerians applying to German universities is planned in Lagos, but no date was given.
stories.tip: Book German visa appointments only through the official consulate and service provider websites, and check often for newly released slots.

stories.headline: Australia may make students park funds in an Australian bank first
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs department is consulting on tougher Genuine Student rules and new proof-of-funds options. Three of the four options would make applicants hold money in an Australian bank account in their own name before applying, from half of total course and living costs up to a full first year. No decision has been made; submissions close on 23 November 2026.
stories.tip: If you plan to study in Australia in 2027, start building documented savings now and watch homeaffairs.gov.au for the final money rules.

stories.headline: Canada keeps 2027 targets: 380,000 new PRs, 150,000 new students
stories.summary: Canada's new immigration plan, released with the federal budget on 5 November, holds permanent resident admissions at 380,000 a year for 2027 to 2029. New temporary arrivals are capped at 370,000 a year, split into 220,000 workers and 150,000 students. Ottawa also plans to give permanent status to many people already in Canada on temporary permits.
stories.tip: Study permit places stay tight, so apply early with a strong study plan and clear proof of funds.

stories.headline: UK sets 10 years as the normal wait for permanent settlement
stories.summary: The Home Secretary told Parliament on 2 November that most migrants will now wait ten years before settling, up from five. Higher earners above £50,271 and some public service workers can still settle after five years, and the top earners after three. Applicants must also show clean records, strong English, no public debts and steady National Insurance payments. No start date was given in the announcement.
stories.tip: If you plan to settle in the UK, keep your pay slips, tax records and English results organised from day one, and watch gov.uk for the start date.

stories.headline: US now requires a health declaration from every air passenger
stories.summary: From 3 November, everyone flying to the United States, whatever their nationality, must sign a CDC form saying they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the previous 21 days. Airlines must check the form before boarding, and it also applies to people connecting through a US airport. The order is set to run until 18 December unless CDC changes it.
stories.tip: Fill in the form at check-in or at the airport, and carry your travel history details in case the airline asks.

stories.headline: UK Budget plans to keep two-year Graduate visa for some universities' students
stories.summary: The 28 October Budget says graduates of universities with strong immigration compliance and good job outcomes will keep a two-year Graduate visa, softening the planned cut to 18 months from 1 January 2027. The government has not yet said which universities qualify, what counts as good outcomes, or when this starts. Until rules are published, the 18-month cut stays the working assumption for applications made from 1 January.
stories.tip: If you finish your course soon, apply for the Graduate visa before 31 December 2026 to lock in two years, and ask your university about its compliance status before you pay a deposit.

stories.headline: Nigeria extends UK passport clinics to 27 November
stories.summary: The Nigeria Immigration Service has pushed its special passport exercise in the UK from 30 October to 27 November 2026. London and Manchester run from 3 to 27 November, while Aberdeen and Cardiff only open from 3 to 6 November. Only people who already booked online are served, and cash is not accepted at the venues.
stories.tip: Book your slot on the High Commission portal now and bring your application form, payment slip, appointment printout, return envelope and old passport.

stories.headline: More Nigerian UK study applications withdrawn as universities fear refusals
stories.summary: A report citing a Financial Times analysis of Home Office data says 22.7% of Nigerian student visa applications were withdrawn in the first half of 2026, up from 4.5% a year earlier. The report links the jump to universities pulling offers early, because they must now keep visa refusals under 5% or risk losing their licence. The figures are secondhand, so treat them as a trend, not an official count.
stories.tip: Hold your CAS and visa application until you have clear funds proof and strong study ties, and confirm your offer is still live before paying deposits.

stories.headline: German missions warn Nigerians: we don't work with visa agents
stories.summary: The German embassy in Abuja and consulate in Lagos said on X that they use no visa agents and that nobody can promise approval, a job or a faster slot. Booking an appointment through the official system costs nothing. The warning followed reports of applicants who paid large sums for fake offers.
stories.tip: Use only the official German mission and VFS pages, and never pay anyone who guarantees a visa or an appointment.

stories.headline: UK and Nigeria vow tougher action on visa fraud and fake documents
stories.summary: After talks in London on 6 October, UK and Nigerian officials agreed to work together on visa fraud, organised immigration crime and better document checks. They also pledged to support safe returns of people who abuse the system. No change to UK visa rules for ordinary Nigerian travellers was announced.
stories.tip: Submit only genuine, verifiable documents and use the official gov.uk site, because forged papers can lead to refusal and long bans.
